A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same M-IDoL study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream classification and segmentation results, component ablations, expert-routing analyses and representation visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a representation visualization for M-IDoL without the routing loss.

M1.justification: Equation 15 adds a minus sign to the routing-consistency loss, correcting the specified training objective. The architecture, routing mechanism and inference procedure remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that the implementation changed or training was rerun.

E1.justification: The documented training datasets, five imaging modalities and 21 evaluated downstream datasets remain the same. The isolated IDRiD split reference disappears from Appendix A, but neither version reports a corresponding dataset entry or experimental result.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds M-IDoL without Lroute as a comparator to the full model. The external baseline sets in Tables 3 and 5 and the other representation comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the stated ISIC2018 split from 7:1.5:1.5 to 7:1:2 and the MIMIC pretraining count from 294,257 to 277,827, matching the existing Table 1 count. ISIC2024 and total pretraining counts decrease by three. These are reported setting corrections; rerunning experiments is not established.

E4.justification: The new Figure 5(i) tests representation separation without Lroute and shows overlapping modality clusters. Existing component and expert-count ablations, loss curves, confusion matrices and Grad-CAM analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three random seeds and use two-sided t-tests between the top two models. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 4 replaces an OCTDL series that duplicated OCTID results: for example, M-IDoL's plotted AUC changes from 99.59 to 99.34, the value already present in Table 5 in both versions. Figure 5 adds the no-Lroute qualitative result. Numerical results in Tables 2, 3 and 5 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the assertion that H(X) remains constant with an approximation under normalized representations and explicitly identifies the independence assumption behind the density-ratio approximation. Appendix B corrects H(X|Y) to H(X|Z). The central information-decomposition derivation is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about information decomposition, modality specificity and diversity, and generalization across 21 downstream datasets.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 recasts the claimed advantage over Unimiss+, LVM-Med and UniMed as an average exceeding 6%, and confines the claimed advantage exceeding 4% over MedCoss and CoSMIC to OCT and pathology. The averaging convention remains unspecified, and Table 5 does not clearly support the 6% statement for every named comparator.

D1.justification: Appendix C removes the stated Mixup/CutMix probability and alpha without replacements; Appendix A removes the CXP selection of 191,229 PA images. v2 adds a direct OCT-TVHL dataset access URL. The implementation repository and principal hardware and optimization details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work positioning and distinct cited research remain unchanged. Dataset references become footnotes, duplicate bibliography entries are consolidated, and LVM-Med publication metadata is corrected; these do not introduce new prior work.

P1.justification: Sentence-level copyediting corrects grammar, terminology and an unfinished sentence in Appendix B. Author order and publication information change, and acknowledgements are added. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 expands from nine to ten panels and relocates its legend. Figure 4 uses taller plots and corrects the OCTDL display; Table 1 moves from page 5 to page 6. Other changes concern sizing, captions and dataset labels.

improvement.justification: v2 improves correctness through the routing-loss sign correction, the repaired OCTDL plot and more consistent dataset reporting. The additional routing-loss ablation and copyediting also help. These are limited gains with unchanged benchmark tables; removed augmentation and sampling details and the unclear aggregate-gain claim leave reproducibility and interpretation weaknesses.
